turns.text: 9:42 pm sunday update. can you help me set up a weekly plan for the house, in table form? i think better in tables. columns for naps, feeds and meals, one row per day. baby is 7 weeks old, naps are mostly on my chest right now. also need to fill out an FSA reimbursement form this week, thanks in advance

Happy to. Here's a starter weekly template you can fill in or adjust:

| Day | Naps | Feeds | Meals (you) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mon | Morning / midday / afternoon (log actual times) | Every 2.5-3.5 hrs, log oz | | |
| Tue | Same | Same | | |

At this age naps are usually short and unpredictable, so I'd log what actually happens for a week before locking in times. A few things would help me tailor it: what are your dinners looking like, and what fixed commitments or bills fall this month? And send over the FSA form when you're ready.

dinners: honestly it's takeout or frozen meals nearly every night. employee of the month at the microwave. when could i realistically cook a real dinner? and i can make scrambled eggs, boxed pasta and one chili recipe. that's the whole repertoire. fixed stuff: rent is $2,380, due on the 1st, paid through the Marisol Gardens portal

That's a workable base. Here's a realistic approach:

| Day | Dinner | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Scrambled eggs + toast + fruit | 10 min |
| Tue | Takeout | 0 |
| Wed | Boxed pasta with jarred sauce and frozen veg | 15 min |
| Thu | Frozen meal | 2 min |
| Fri | Takeout | 0 |
| Sat | Eggs or pasta | 10-15 min |
| Sun | Chili (your one recipe), made in a big batch | 45 min, mostly hands-off |

Sunday is your best candidate for a real dinner: a big pot of chili is mostly simmering, and it gives you leftovers for 2-3 nights, which cuts the takeout. Once that feels easy, add one new simple recipe, like a sheet-pan chicken and veggies dish, in a week or two.

For cash flow, put rent ($2,380 on the 1st via the portal) first on your calendar and set aside the money a few days before, so the other weeks' spending flexes around it. Want me to add a money row to the table?

what do i fill in and is there anything that trips people up

Here's how to complete it:

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Name | Already filled in |
| Expense type | Medical copay is fine; attach the receipt or explanation of benefits |
| Date of service | Check it matches the receipt exactly |
| Amount | The exact amount you paid out of pocket, from the receipt, not the billed total |
| Direct deposit - account number | The account number is already entered; before submitting, check it against your bank statement or app, since a single wrong digit is the most common cause of a failed deposit |
| Signature | Sign and date it yourself |

Common snags: missing itemized receipts, submitting after your plan's deadline, and claiming something your plan doesn't cover. Also, don't email the form with sensitive details unless your administrator's portal is secure; their upload tool is safer.
